question.text: A block of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> is placed on a rough inclined plane. The inclination of the plane is gradually increased until the block just begins to slide down. The sin of angle made by the plane with horizontal is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac></math> when the block start sliding. The coefficient of friction between the block and the plane is (<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mo> </mo><mo>=</mo><mo> </mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>)

solution.text:
The block will just start sliding when the angle θ made by the inclined plane with the horizontal will be equal to the angle of repose.

θ=θrepose=tan-1μ

⇒tanθ=μ
μ=34
